steps.body: Mass converts identically: a kilogram holds 1,000 grams, so 5 kg is 5,000 g. Only the factor changes from one quantity to the next.
steps.narration: Mass converts identically: a kilogram holds 1,000 grams, so 5 kg is 5,000 g. Only the factor changes from one quantity to the next.

widget.prompt: How many grams in 3 kilograms? Hop one kilogram at a time.

commonLandings.feedback: Two hops reach 2,000 g; the pack is three kilograms.
Four hops overshoot — three kilograms is 3,000 grams.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10. From 430, 3 hops land on 460.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — each kilogram is 1,000 grams, so three reach 3,000.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — three kilograms stops exactly at 3,000 grams.

cml.actionGoal: Hold the quantity fixed while the unit changes, and watch which way the NUMBER moves for g4v mass.
invariants: Converting never changes how much there is: a smaller unit needs more of them and a bigger unit needs fewer, so the number moves in the opposite direction to the unit size in g4v mass.
misconceptions: Multiplying when converting to a bigger unit, adding the conversion factor instead of multiplying by it, or comparing bare numbers across different units.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If the unit got ten times smaller, what would happen to the number that measures the same object?

widget.prompt: A pack measures 9 kilograms, and each kilogram is 1000 grams. Compute 9 × 1000.

commonErrors.feedback: Adding mixes a quantity with a rate. Each of the 9 kilograms contributes 1000 grams, so they multiply.
That divided. Going to the SMALLER unit needs more of them, so the number must grow.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Name the quantity and the conversion factor, then decide whether the count should grow or shrink.

widget.prompt: Converting 5 kilograms into grams, do you multiply or divide by 1,000?

options.label: Multiply — grams are smaller, so there are more of them
options.feedback: Correct — each kilogram contains 1,000 grams, so 5 kilograms is 5,000 grams.

options.label: Divide — the number should get smaller
options.feedback: Dividing would give 0.005, which is far less than the mass you started with.

options.label: Neither — the number stays the same
options.feedback: The mass stays the same, but the NUMBER must change because the unit changed.

options.label: Multiply by 100
options.feedback: 100 is the centimeters-per-meter factor; a kilogram holds 1,000 grams.
